name: MonarchAccordion
title: Accordion
summary: Stacked sections whose content opens under each header, one at a time or any number, with headers that are headings and buttons.
whenToUse: For a set of related sections people scan by title and open one by one: FAQs, settings groups, the details of a record.
whenNotToUse: For one section on its own use MonarchCollapsible. For content people need to compare side by side, show it open or use tabs. For navigation to other screens use list rows.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAccordion(items: List<MonarchAccordionItem>, expanded: Set<String>, onExpandedChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, multiple: Boolean = false, collapsible: Boolean = true, enabled: Boolean = true, trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, expandedLabel: String? = null, collapsedLabel: String? = null, content: @Composable ColumnScope.(item: MonarchAccordionItem) -> Unit)
class MonarchAccordionItem(id: String, title: String, enabled: Boolean = true)

options.name: items
options.description: The sections in order: id, title and whether the section can be opened.

options.name: expanded
options.description: The ids of the open sections.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new set of open ids when a header is activated.

options.name: multiple
options.description: Lets any number of sections stay open (the web's type multiple). Without it opening one closes the others.

options.name: collapsible
options.description: One-at-a-time only: lets the open section's header close it again (the web's collapsible).

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether any section can be opened or closed.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: An icon at the end of each header, such as a chevron; it turns half a turn while open. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: content
options.description: The content of a section, in the muted body style.

options.name: headerTrailing
options.description: Content at the end of a header, such as a count; part of the header button.

options.name: MonarchAccordionItem.subtitle
options.description: A second line under the title, read after it.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: Only the header; its state is "Collapsed" and it offers the expand action.

states.name: expanded
states.description: The content under the header; the trailing icon turned half a turn; the state "Expanded" and the collapse action when the section can be closed.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The header in the disabled text color; it does not open or close.

appearance: Headers use the strong body style in the default text color and the trailing icon in the muted text color; content uses the body style in the muted text color. Lines in the default border color sit above the first section and under each section. Disabled headers use the disabled text color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Material 3 has no accordion, so Monarch builds one; iOS styles the system DisclosureGroup instead and ships no accordion type. The web Accordion is Radix Accordion with separate Item, Trigger and Content parts and headingAs; here the sections are data (MonarchAccordionItem) and the content a lambda per item, and every header is a heading without levels (Compose has one heading property). Arrow-key, Home and End movement between headers is not offered; focus and TalkBack move header by header. The web is controlled or uncontrolled; here state is hoisted as a set of ids for both modes. The header is built here rather than with MonarchCollapsible because MonarchCollapsible's header cannot be marked as a heading; the behavior (button role, state, expand and collapse actions, reduced motion) is the same. The chevron is a slot because Monarch bundles no icons. Closed content leaves the composition, as in MonarchCollapsible and on iOS.
accessibility: Each header is one element with the Button role and the heading property, so TalkBack's heading navigation reaches it.
Each header has the state description "Expanded" or "Collapsed" and the expand or collapse accessibility action; an open section that cannot be closed offers no collapse action.
Headers are at least 56dp high and span the width, so the touch target is well over 48dp.
Closed content leaves the composition, so TalkBack does not reach it.
Content grows into place, or appears at once when animations are off.
The title wraps at font scale 2.0 and the trailing icon stays at the end in both layout directions.
edgeCases: With multiple, ids that are not in items are kept in the reported set; one at a time, opening a section replaces the whole set with its id.
With collapsible false and nothing open, any header opens its section; the open one then stays open until another is opened.
State inside closed content is lost; hoist it.

examples.title: Single, collapsible
examples.template:
MonarchAccordion(
    items = listOf(
        MonarchAccordionItem({{items.0.id}}, {{items.0.title}}),
        MonarchAccordionItem({{items.1.id}}, {{items.1.title}}),
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    trailingIcon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.ChevronDown, contentDescription = null) },
) { item ->
    Text(if (item.id == {{items.0.id}}) {{items.0.body}} else {{items.1.body}})
}
examples.code:
MonarchAccordion(
    items = listOf(
        MonarchAccordionItem("billing", "When am I billed?"),
        MonarchAccordionItem("cancel", "Can I cancel at any time?"),
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    trailingIcon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.ChevronDown, contentDescription = null) },
) { item ->
    Text(if (item.id == "billing") "On the first of each month, for the seats in use." else "Yes. Access continues to the end of the paid period.")
}

examples.title: Any number open, with a chevron
examples.code:
MonarchAccordion(
    items = listOf(MonarchAccordionItem("profile", "Profile"), MonarchAccordionItem("security", "Security")),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    multiple = true,
    trailingIcon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.ChevronDown, contentDescription = null) },
) { item ->
    Text("Settings of ${item.title}")
}
